The island of Sol’Kesh, with its coral-strewn shores and single dominating mountain range is a land untouched and unknown. 
Encouraging Travelers to set their footprint upon it to explore its depths and discover all the beauty and danger that this primal land 
has to offer.
Researching the flora and fauna that thrive within these lands is not only for bookish scholars, understanding the perils one may 
endure while stepping into the thick mire of a mile wide swamp is vastly more safe when one knows which creatures lurk beneath the 
murky waters, and how to avoid them. Travelers that keep notes on their discoveries, who share their findings with others, and strive 
to understand the life that surrounds them often have a way of staying alive long enough to benefit from their research.
A Traveler's Journal can take on many forms: A loose bunch of scribbled notes - more mud and blood than ink, a hard-bound tome 
full of illustrations and meticulous script, or carved pictograms in the soft underside of argustaur shell. What is important is that the 
Travelers note their findings and learn from them. In some unfortunate cases, these dirt soiled papers are all that's left in a mouldering 
pile of bone and traveling gear. While an ignoble end for the writer, another Traveler chancing upon these notes would not only be 
warned of the dangers that await them, but can build off of them to learn more about the creatures that dwell nearby.
Writing a Creature Journal Entry is more than a narrative activity for a Traveler to take part in, writing and finishing creature Journal 
Entries impart benefits in dealing with the subject creature in both aggressive and peaceful ways. Traveler's Journal's can be completed 
in all manner of ways, this could be a shared endeavor between a party of Travelers, a singular quest of knowledge, an accumulation of 
notes found in dusty libraries or inscribed from the ramblings of madmen. If a Traveler wants to write a creature Journal Entry, they 
should discuss their goals with their Keeper, and together work out the best method to complete it. The most important aspect to keep 
in mind, is that this is about exploration and potentially benefiting from their discoveries.

Journal Completion steps can be completed in any order. 
If a Traveler fails to complete a step, by either failing to succeed

again, but only with a new encounter of the same creature type.

Journaling a Traveler’s Discoveries
The beetle patrols thin branches 
in the Wealdwoods, farming the 
dewdrop aphids with its specialized 
proboscis. When confronted with 
others of its kind, it defends its little 
herd with the numerous spines that 
fan out from its abdomen 
Very few thoughts go on behind 
the young gastropod's single 
large eye. As hundreds hatch 
at once, scuttling on the beach 
to scavenge scraps, only a few 
grow old enough to show a 
glimmer of cunning
A thick mass of slime mold 
slowly inches along damp 
Umbrawells floors, its bulbs 
letting loose a trickle of spores 
along in its creeping wake
A heady aroma wafts through the air, attracting 
twull snails from far across the Farplains for a 
nibble. As the snails congregate onto the large 
leaves, piling up in large numbers, the plant's 
true motives become clear as hectatrex wander 
over and pluck their choice snails off the plant,
all the while brushing up against the tall
plants flower and carrying its pollen 
over to the next snail trap
A steady stream of opaque fumes spreads from 
the beetle's highly adapted pygidium through 
the Wealdwoods undergrowth. Obscuring the 
fetaur from any aerial carnivores so it may 
chew through the rotten mulch in peace
